headline: Mastercard ties Agent Pay to its OpenAI deal and signs a Tencent MoU
body: Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach said on the Oct. 29 earnings call that a broad OpenAI agreement includes Agent Pay and "goes well beyond" it. On Nov. 2, Mastercard signed a memorandum of understanding with TenPay Global, Tencent's cross-border payment platform, to explore agentic payments.
note: Miebach named trust as the gating factor, saying consumers need to feel comfortable and that a registered agent matters. The Tencent MoU commits the two sides to explore the idea, and nothing more is stated.

evidence.text: Lost in the recent earnings announcement from Mastercard was a broad strategic partnership with OpenAI that Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach said includes the use of his company’s Agent Pay and “goes well beyond.”
“Our agreement establishes collaboration across payments, joint services growth and AI transformation,” Miebach said during the Thursday (Oct. 29) earnings call .
Mastercard Agent Pay is the company’s infrastructure for enabling payments in agentic commerce, according to a page on its website.
“One of the things that need to happen before this to really take off is consumers need to feel comfortable,” Miebach said.
“Use of Agent Pay and having a registered agent is a key thing.

Mastercard announced another partnership Monday (Nov. 2), saying in a press release that the company and Tencent ’s cross-border payment platform, TenPay Global , will explore new opportunities in agentic payments as well as greater cross-border payment interoperability.

Mastercard and TenPay Global signed a memorandum of understanding for a proposed collaboration that spans QR acceptance for international visitors in the Chinese mainland, remittances into the Weixin / WeChat ecosystem and AI-enabled commerce, according to the release.
